statement: In our case, since SIZE(dc ) has 2poly(d) functions, naively computing the dimension-(2d − k) homology of SSIZE(dc )∪{3SATd } for any constant k requires computing the ranks of two 2poly(d) - sized matrix, which is already superpolynomial time in 2d , violating the “constructiveness” of natural proofs. It is unknown whether the “largeness” condition is also violated, but, for any fixed dimension r, we conjecture that the probability a random total function f changes the dimension r homology of SSIZE(dc ) is exponentially small.
